key_insight: Individualized functional-network attribution in ADNI showed a modest person-specific component atop a strong population-shared pattern.
clinical_relevance: This cognitive-prediction study, not cancer drug discovery research, cautions against treating individualized rs-fMRI attribution as a validated person-specific clinical biomarker.
method: Evaluated per-subject network-ablation attribution for a frozen Schaefer-200 functional-connectivity model predicting MMSE and ADAS-Cog13.
Compared within-session split-half reliability with scan-rescan reliability.
Used a mismatched-subject permutation null to assess individual specificity.
evidence_signal: The predictor was trained on 875 ADNI participants; attribution correlations were approximately 0.95 for split-half, 0.61 for scan-rescan, and 0.46–0.47 under the mismatched-subject null, with matched pairs significantly exceeding the null.
watch_item: High within-session reliability can overstate individual specificity; scan-rescan reliability and permutation-null controls should be reported together.
paper_title: How Reliable Is Individualized Functional-Network Attribution in Resting-State fMRI Cognitive Prediction in ADNI?
